item.body:
### Summary
As a reader, I want the "…" at the top right of a member's message to open that post's action menu: Citer, Ajouter à la citation, Alerter, and so on. Today it opens a "link" popup at the top centre. Operator report after a device test, 2026-11-07. **M4**.

### To analyse (read-only, before any fix)
- How the reader wires the per-message "…": LOT-087 message actions (#179, done), `reader.js` and the bridge, and the LOT-186 changes merged today.
- What legacy shows @ 2440d79: the message action sheet in `MessagesView.swift`.
- Find why a "link" popup appears instead. Candidates: a link-preview or context menu, or a tap routed to the link handler (LOT-137).
- Check whether this is related to #566 (reader lifecycle) or #575.

comments.body:
## Analysis (read-only, sub-orch) 2026-11-07

Read from `origin/dev-swift` @ `4b1e77f`; legacy @ `2440d79`.

### Current code path of the per-message "⋯"
1. **HTML.** `TopicHTMLBuilder.swift:148-151` writes `<button type="button" class="menu-button" data-menu="message" data-post="N">⋯</button>`. It is a `<button>`, not an `<a>`, so WebKit has no link to preview or long-press. The header sits outside `.content`. This rules out the "the ⋯ is a link" candidate.
2. **JS.** `reader.js:80-86`: the document click listener (in the app's content world) matches `button[data-menu]` and posts `{type:"menu", post, source:"message"}`. It never reaches `decidePolicyFor`, so the LOT-137 link router (`ReaderWebController.swift:342-353` → `TopicReaderView.swift:275-283`) is **not** involved. This rules out "routed to the link handler".
3. **Bridge.** `ReaderBridgeMessage.swift:83-86` → `ReaderWebController.handle` `:220-222` → `events.menu` → `TopicReaderView.swift:288` → `openMenu` (`TopicReaderModel+Quote.swift:72`) → `requestMenu` (`TopicReaderModel+Menu.swift:69-75`). The entries are the policy's (`MessageMenuAction.swift` `MessageMenuPolicy`) **minus every action with no registered handler** (`MessageActionRegistry.swift:298-306`).
4. **Presentation.** `TopicReaderView.swift:122-132`: a SwiftUI `.confirmationDialog`, `titleVisibility: .hidden`, attached to the **whole reader view**, with no anchor.

### Why a "link" popup at the top centre (most likely cause)
Two facts together give exactly what the report describes:
- **Position.** Since iOS 26, a `confirmationDialog` is presented as a popover-style sheet from the view it is attached to. Here that view is the full-screen reader (`TopicReaderView` body), not the "⋯". The sheet therefore anchors to the reader's frame, which puts it at the top centre, far from the tapped button.
- **Content.** The handlers installed are only those in `TopicReaderView.swift:247-266`: `LinkActionHandler` always, plus the two quote handlers (only when `canQuote`: `quoting != nil && replyTarget != nil`, `TopicReaderModel+Quote.swift:124`), `FavoriteActionHandler` (only with `services.flagActions`), and Editer/Supprimer (only with a composer, own posts).
  - "Alerter" has no handler: LOT-135 #225 is `status: ready`, not done.
  - AQ (LOT-134) and Bookmark (LOT-132) have none either.
  - So on any page without the answer form, or with no composer, or with no flag actions, the dialog shows **one row, "Link"** (title hidden). That is the "link popup".
  - A private conversation reached by a followed link has `composer: nil` (`TopicReaderView.swift:140`), so its menu shows only "Link" too.
- **Lifetime trap (secondary, to confirm).** `installMenuActions()` runs once, in the first `.task` (`:159-162`). It reads `composer` and `services.flagActions` at that moment. A reader created before the session was restored keeps a Link-only registry until it is recreated: nothing re-runs it when `composer` changes.

**Device check needed to confirm.** Was the operator logged in? Was it a public topic with an answer form, or an MP? How many rows did the popup show? Logging `presentedMenu.entries` with #575's `ReaderLog` would settle it.

### What LOT-186 changed
`contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior = .never` plus `obscuredInsets` (`ReaderWebController.swift:64-67, 113`) puts the page under the glass bars.
- A "⋯" scrolled under the top bar is covered by the bar, so a tap there does nothing.
- It cannot produce a link popup.

LOT-186 is not the cause. It is not #566 / #575 (lifecycle) either.

### Legacy @ 2440d79
- `MessagesView.swift:1521-1569` `presentPopupMenu`: the message menu is a **`UIEditMenuInteraction` anchored at the tapped point**.
- `popupAnchor` `:1571-1595` takes the JS viewport offsets, adds the insets, and sets the arrow up or down.
- Title "Post de <pseudo>" (`:1597-1610`); entries `:1612-1800`; policy `:196-290`.
- Legacy shows the full list (Citer, Citer ☐, Favoris, Link (share sheet), Alerter (form or mail fallback), AQ, Bookmark, Editer, Supprimer) because every action was wired.

### Proposed fix
1. **Anchor the menu on the "⋯".**
   - `reader.js` adds the button's `getBoundingClientRect()` (four numbers) to the `menu` message.
   - `ReaderBridgeMessage` decodes them, finite and clamped to the viewport, ignored otherwise.
   - The controller converts them to web-view coordinates (plus `obscuredInsets.top`).
   - Then either (a) a `UIEditMenuInteraction` on the web view, as legacy does, or (b) a SwiftUI `.popover(attachmentAnchor: .rect(...))` with `presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)` and a button list.
   - (b) keeps the LOT-087 learning: give the action the menu it was shown for.
2. **Title "Post de <pseudo>".** As legacy: `titleVisibility: .visible`, or the menu title. Without it, a one-row popup reads as an unexplained "Link".
3. **Rebuild the registry when `composer` or `flagActions` change.** Use `.task(id:)` on an identity of both, so a reader opened before login completion gets the quote, flag and edit handlers.
4. **Not in this fix.** "Alerter" comes with LOT-135 #225, "AQ" with LOT-134, "Bookmark" with LOT-132. Say so in the PR so the device check expects them missing.

Tests:
- bridge decoding of the rect (non-finite, negative and huge values rejected);
- the registry rebuilt after a composer change;
- an app-hosted `WKWebView` test that a click on `.menu-button` posts `menu` with a rect.

### Scope, effort, routing, conflicts
- **Scope.** `reader.js` (menu message), `ReaderBridgeMessage.swift`, `ReaderWebController.swift` (`Events.menu` signature), `TopicReaderView.swift` (dialog → anchored menu, `installMenuActions` trigger), `TopicReaderModel+Menu.swift`. Update the LOT-087 spec (differences) and the GAP-064 row.
- **Effort.** Medium (about 1 session plus a Mac check).
- **Routing.** Sonnet 5.5 author → Opus 5.5 review (UI wiring of an existing, specified menu). Use Opus → Fable if (a) `UIEditMenuInteraction` is chosen, since that is UIKit inside the web view.
- **Conflicts.**
  - **#575** rewrites `ReaderWebController.swift` (+105/−113), moves the delegates and proxies to `ReaderWebController+Navigation.swift`, and edits `TopicReaderView.swift`. Land #575 first, then branch.
  - **#583** only touches the toolbar block of `TopicReaderView.swift` and `ReaderPageControls.swift`. That is a low conflict risk (a different block).
  - **#595** touches the same `reader.js` click handler, the bridge and `installMenuActions`. Do #594 first, then #595, in the same session if possible.

comments.body:
## Device check (mac/m2-lead repro) 2026-11-07: the analysis is confirmed

**Builds**: `f9901d9` (origin/dev-swift, with #575) for every row, plus `4b1e77f` for the row marked †. **Devices**: iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0, portrait; iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator, iOS 27.0, landscape. UI-test driven: a tap on the post's "…", then the popup's rows read from the accessibility tree. Every screenshot was looked at; none is published because they show forum content. Harness note: the logged-in builds were signed ad hoc (`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=-`) instead of unsigned, because an unsigned build cannot use the keychain.

| Device | Session | Page | Rows in the popup | Where the popup sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | logged out † | public topic | **1: "Link"** | top centre, under the nav bar, arrow pointing down; the tapped "…" was at the right edge, lower down |
| iPhone | logged out | public topic, last page | **1: "Link"** | top centre (popover 81,62 240×93 pt), arrow pointing down; the "…" tapped was at 358,167 pt, at the right edge |
| iPad | logged out | public topic | **1: "Link"** | popover over the **topic list column**, pointing at the reader's left edge; the "…" was at the far right of the reader |
| iPhone | logged in | public topic with an answer form | **4: Citer, Citer ☐, Favoris, Link** | top centre (popover 81,62 240×261 pt) while the "…" was at 358,480 pt |
| iPad | logged in | public topic with an answer form | **4: Citer, Citer ☐, Favoris, Link** | same anchoring as logged out |
| iPhone | logged in | **MP** (a read group conversation, someone else's post) | **3: Citer, Citer ☐, Link** | top centre |

The dialog has no title in all cases ("Post de …" is missing).

So both parts of the analysis hold:
- **Content.** Logged out, the only action with a handler is "Link", so the popup is a single "Link" row. That is the "link popup" of the report. Logged in, the quote and flag handlers add rows. "Alerter", AQ and Bookmark are never there.
- **Position.** The `confirmationDialog` is anchored to the whole reader: top centre on iPhone, over the list column on iPad. It never points at the "…".

Not covered here:
- My own post (Editer and Supprimer). No write was allowed, and the posts tapped were not the account's.
- An MP reached through a followed link (`composer: nil`).
- The "registry built before login" trap. Every logged-in run started with the session already restored.

### Side finding: the first post's "…" cannot be reached
At the top of a page, the **first post's header (avatar, pseudo, date, "…") sits under the status bar and the top glass bar**. Its "…" is at y = 5–53 pt, and the bar ends near 115 pt on iPhone. A pull-down does not reveal it. A tap where it sits opens nothing.
- On a one-post topic, no "…" can be reached at all.
- Seen on iPhone (logged out and logged in) and on iPad, on `f9901d9`.
- It looks like LOT-186 (#552, page under the bars). It is filed as #641.

## Operator request, 2026-11-08: keep the per-post "+" menu (M4) The operator asks to keep the menu at the top right of each post, which users rely on. He says its behaviour "can be tweaked in Settings". **The operator puts this in M4.** This issue (with GAP-064 / LOT-087) already covers the menu itself, so this is a comment and not a new issue. ### What the legacy code shows @ 2440d79 - **Button.** `SuperHFRplus/Assets/HTML/templatev2.htm:6`: `
+
`. The date (`:7`) and the empty end of the header band (`:8`) open the same menu. - **Entries.** `HFRswift/Swift/MessagesView.swift:196-275` (`MessagePopupMenuPolicy`, the `.message` source), sorted by `:277-306`: Citer, Citer ☐/☑, Editer, Favoris, Link, Alerter, AQ, Bookmark, Supprimer. The ObjC twin is `HFRswift/Wrapped/MessagesTableViewController.m:2083-2201`. - **Settings.** No setting configures the "+" menu itself. The only setting that changes its content is **"Activer le stockage MP"**: - key `mpstorage_active`: `AppSettingsView.swift:107, 465`; - it gates **Bookmark**: `Classes/ObjCMessageActionsBuilder.m:18` (also never in MPs), and `MessagesTableViewController.m:2194-2197`. - AQ is hidden in MPs (`ObjCMessageActionsBuilder.m:19`). - Nothing else in `AppSettingsView.swift:86-109` or in `InAppSettings.bundle` (`Root.inApp.plist`, `Advanced.plist`) touches it. - **Not the "+" menu.** The keys `actionsmesages_*` (`Classes/OnlineMessagesTableViewController.m:777-806`) are a different menu: the topic-level actions (first page, last page…). They have no settings UI at 2440d79. - **Unclear.** Which setting does the operator mean? `mpstorage_active` (Bookmark) is the only one found. **To confirm with the operator** before anything is added. ### SwiftHFR today (origin/dev-swift @ d09a0ad8) - **The menu exists.** The button is `⋯`, not `+` (`App/SwiftHFR/Reader/TopicHTMLBuilder.swift:148`; GAP-051 records the header change as `b`). It opens a popover anchored on the button (#608). - **Missing entries.** Alerter, AQ and Bookmark wait for LOT-135, LOT-134 and LOT-132 (GAP-064). The bookmark handler must keep legacy's `mpstorage_active` gate (`MessageMenuAction.swift:115-116`, `canBookmark`). - **Open question for the operator.** Should the glyph go back to `+`, as in legacy? That would turn the GAP-051 header change from `b` into a parity item. Related: #645 (reader "…" overflow menu, not this per-post menu), #652 (avatar/pseudo → profile).

Operator, 2026-11-08 (answers to the questions above):
- The tweakable "+" is the floating reply button at the bottom of a topic or MP page, with the setting **Bouton +** (Réponse rapide, Répondre comme le forum, Pas d'icône): tracked in #654. It exists on legacy `master` @ `21173e77`, not at `2440d79`.
- On each post, the operator wants the **"+"** back instead of "⋯" (reverses the GAP-051 change).
Label `beta-test finding`, M4.
